```{r echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

# An Example

```{r}
library(R6)
RectangleR6 <- R6Class("RectangleR6", list(
  width = 0,
  height = 0,
  area = function() {
    return(self$width * self$height)
  })
)
```

`self` refers to the object itself


# Constructor and Immutability

For free, function `new` 

```{r}
x <- RectangleR6$new()
x
```

`clone` function - used for copying, but by default objects are immutable.

```{r}
y <- x
y$width <- 5
x$width
```
# `initialize`

replaces the default behavior of `new`, i.e. we can check for validity:


```{r}
RectangleR6 <- R6Class("RectangleR6", list(
  width = 0,
  height = 0,
  initialize = function(width, height) {
    stopifnot(width >= 0, height >= 0)
    self$width = width
    self$height = height
  },
  area = function() {
    return(self$width * self$height)
  })
)
```

# Adding Methods

```{r}
RectangleR6$set("public", "expand_by", function(w=0, h=0) {
    stopifnot(w >= 0, h >= 0)
    self$width = self$width + w
    self$height = self$height + h
    invisible(self)
})
```

```{r}
x_new <- RectangleR6$new(3,4)
x_new
```

# This needs care!

- Only newly created objects have the functionality:

```{r error=TRUE}
x$expand_by(2,3)
```
- _Convention_: if the function is implemented for the side effect, return `self` invisibly. This allows chaining.

# Chaining

R6 classes allow chaining

```{r}
x_new$expand_by(1,2)$expand_by(3,2) 
```

same as 

```{r}
x_new$
  expand_by(1,2)$
  expand_by(3,2) |> print()
```

# R6 reference class

```{r eval=FALSE}
R6Class(
  classname = NULL,
  public = list(),
  private = NULL,
  active = NULL,
  inherit = NULL,
  lock_objects = TRUE,
  class = TRUE,
  portable = TRUE,
  lock_class = FALSE,
  cloneable = TRUE,
  parent_env = parent.frame()
)
```

```{r}
source("../../code/2026-04-14-code.R")

widths <- abs(rnorm(1000))
heights <- abs(rnorm(1000))

make_R6_area <- function(widths, heights) {
  result <- numeric(length(widths))
  for (i in 1:length(widths)) {
    rectangle <- RectangleR6$new(widths[i],
                                 heights[i])
    result[i] <- rectangle$area()
  }
  result
}


bench <- microbenchmark::microbenchmark(

  make_S4_area(widths, heights), 
  make_R6_area(widths, heights))
```

# Active fields

Help us prevent misuse like this:

```{r}
x$height <- 1
x$width <- -100
x
```
Idea: make height and width private and use active fields to access them

# a new class ...

```{r}
RectangleR6 <- R6Class("RectangleR6", 
  private = list(
    .width = 0,
    .height = 0
  ),
  public = list(initialize = function(width, height) {
    stopifnot(width >= 0, height >= 0)
    private$.width = width             #<<
    private$.height = height           #<<
  },
  area = function() {
    return(private$.width * private$.height)
  }),
  active = list(
    width = function(value) {
      if (missing(value)) {
        private$.width
      } else {
        if (value < 0)
          stop("`$width` can't be negative", call. = FALSE)
        private$.width <- value
      }
    },
    height = function(value) {
      if (missing(value)) {
        private$.height
      } else {
        if (value < 0)
          stop("`$height` can't be negative", call. = FALSE)
        private$.height <- value
      }
    }
  )
)

```

# Active fields ...

- look like fields to the outside

- are implemented using active bindings; their values are re-computed every time 
they are accessed

```{r error=TRUE}
x <- RectangleR6$new(3,5)
x$width

x$width <- 4
x$width <- -1
```
